newsitem.title: USA: Coastal well positioned to meet 15 pct goal.
newsitem.headline: Coastal well positioned to meet 15 pct goal.

text.p: Coastal Corp said Monday it is well positioned to meet once again its target of at least 15 percent annual growth.

The company said first quarter earnings before a refinancing charge were a record $101.2 million, or $0.91 per share, up 23 percent from last year's $82.5 million, or $0.74 per share. This year's first quarter net income, however, was $10.6 million, or $0.06 per share.
Coastal said it took an extraordinary charge of $90.6 million, or $0.85 per share, related to the refinancing of $798 million of higher cost debt to further reduce interest costs.

The company said its increased exploration and production investments "especially paid off. Production of natural gas increased dramatically, reflecting our successful drilling program, with new volumes coming on line in concert with higher prices being realized."

At the end of the first quarter, Coastal said, its subsidiaries were averaging natural gas production of more than 500 million cubic feet daily and "are on-target for further growth as the year progresses."

As part of the merger of Coastal's unregulated natural gas marketing units with similar operations of Westcoast Energy Inc , to form Engage Energy, Coastal received an equalization payment which added $42 million to operating profits, the company said.
It reported first quarter operating profit of $220.0 million compared to $198.6 million last year.

The company noted falling product, crude oil and chemical prices and a mild winter in the U.S. northeast plagued the refining, marketing and chemical industry during the first quarter. At Coastal, it said, this led to "significant declines in inventory values.
"However, improving margins in recent weeks and wider sweet-sour crude oil price differentials indicate that Coastal has the proper strategy in this segment.
"These market trends are favorable for companies like ours which have significant sour and heavy crude oil refining capabilities," it explained.
